description: ol-undefined-var (issue #825): an EAGER block — a control form's own body, which runs where it is written — sees its enclosing scope only as far as that scope has got. spec/tooling.md:184 names this exact case in the Layer 2 semantic-checking table: "a block's read of an enclosing binding created later" is `ol-undefined-var`. No execution order rescues it, because the `repeat` body runs before line 2. Measured: `execute()` raises the same code on this program, so the two stages agree. The contrasting deferred case is tests/conformance/interaction-events/check/deferred-handler-sees-a-later-enclosing-binding, which is byte-similar and must stay CLEAN — the pair is the whole eager/deferred distinction, and it lives in fixtures rather than only in TypeScript so a second implementation inherits it.
